Jack Heart, 2026-11-13, on the design's five open points, asked again today. Write these into this worktree's scratch/design-train-api.md "Open" section; the Manabot worktree's copy already has them.

1. The name `track`: stands. His `tracked_run?` / `track_run?` were to avoid two classes named `Run`; "ok, RunRequest works" solved that. He has not said "keep track" in words, so do not record it as his choice.
2. `etude continue` with only the target changed: he chose "Both". `--resume RUN --until ...` extends the same run; `continue` stays for anything that changes config and makes a child run. Rule: the same config and seed is the same run. A finished run must be reopenable to a further target.
3. Games in flight: he chose "Show how to keep them". The docs carry a worked example of keeping pending games by passing an object that holds them to `run.resume`.
4. The public non-Magic example: he gave no answer. Proceed with a tiny game shipped with Etude, also used for the two-model acceptance example; keep it listed as unanswered.
5. When `run.save()` writes outside a stop: he gave no answer. Proceed with wall time by default, step count when `every=` is given; keep it listed as unanswered.

He also said "i thought we clarified a lot of this". What he did settle today is the naming (RunRequest, RunAttempt, one RunRecord, one CheckpointRecord plus a reference, player, outcome.json, etude.tracking, experiment and cohort, all renaming before release) and that the launcher supplies the experiment name. Those are in the design's Names and Cloud sections.

On the interrupted-save finding: your reading of "local storage probably fine, but ideally avoid remote extra storage" (a snapshot with a pointer published last, unchanged files not re-uploaded, the superseded snapshot deleted once the new pointer is published) fits what he asked of state today: ordinary files readable in place, owned by the author. I have no further words from him on it.
